messages:
incident-bot: INCIDENT ⚠️ AZ-c private subnets: spike in 5xx (NAT failures) across eu-west. paging: @maya_oncall. auto-escalation to SRE. summary: ~8% of requests from eu-west-1 hitting private subnets see 502/504.

maya_oncall: I’m on it, jumping in. any recent infra changes in AZ-c?

tina_sre: saw a Terraform apply ~2h ago that touched route tables for azc-private-subnet-* (PR #2984). Noted new route for ::/0 pointing to a custom gateway id gw-0abcde (looks like NAT64 connector) — that gateway is reporting unhealthy in cloud console. IPv4 default route still points at nat-07f..

jay_infra: confirming: `aws ec2 describe-route-tables --filters Name=tag:Name,Values=azc-private-subnet-*` output snippet:
```
{ Routes: [ { DestinationCidrBlock: "0.0.0.0/0", NatGatewayId: "nat-07f123" }, { DestinationIpv6CidrBlock: "::/0", GatewayId: "gw-0abcde" } ] }
```
Gateway gw-0abcde was created by an older template (nat64 service) and never promoted to prod in AZ-c. Terraform drift attached it during the recent rollout.

lisa_support: Customer impact: support tickets show app endpoints returning 502 and some uploads timing out. APM shows increased latencies and retries specifically for requests that go to services using IPv6 resolver records. We have ~23 customers seeing errors (mostly EU).

maya_oncall: thanks. mitigation plan — rollback the IPv6 route -> point ::/0 to the same egress path as IPv4 (or remove if not required) and fail open to IPv4 only. Is that safe?

tina_sre: safe short-term. Two options: 1) remove the ::/0 route entry (requests will fall back to IPv4), 2) update gateway target to an active translator. Option 1 is fastest.

jay_infra: I can run a one-line change via console/CLI. CLI patch: `aws ec2 replace-route --route-table-id rtb-0a1b2c --destination-ipv6-cidr-block ::/0 --gateway-id none` (or use `delete-route`). I'll do a `--dry-run` then execute. Will annotate TF after emergency change to avoid drift.

maya_oncall: please run and report. Also start page to oncall-sre-followups channel for postmortem. Set incident severity to Sev2.

jay_infra: running dry-run... dry-run success. executing delete-route now.

deploy-bot: deploy job #3129 started by jay_infra for emergency route delete.

jay_infra: delete-route returned OK. Removed IPv6 route entry from rtb-0a1b2c.

incident-bot: Metrics update: 2min after change 5xx rate dropped from 8% -> 0.7% in eu-west. Error traces show IPv6-timeouts reduced.

lisa_support: support dashboard updated: open tickets decreased, customers reporting success. Marking impacted customers notified via in-app banner? We can target those 23 customers.

maya_oncall: good. next: create a Terraform-safe fix — add tf ignore for that route or update module to only apply IPv6 route when gateway is healthy. Also schedule a controlled rollout for nat64 connector with healthchecks. Assign owners?

tina_sre: assigning to eng-infra (jay) for the immediate tf change, and eng-runtime for validating IPv6 behavior with NAT64 (tina will cc runtime).

jay_infra: will open emergency PR to revert the route change and add a precondition check: `data.aws_ec2_transit_gateway_attachment` health check or `aws_route` conditional. PR link: <https://git.internal/repo/infra/pull/3001>.

maya_oncall: handoff: I’ll stay for 30 minutes for flame checks, then hand to tina for postmortem write-up. If anything regresses, page the full SRE rotation.

tina_sre: taking over at 2765432265 for post-incident. Immediate notes for postmortem: root cause = terraform applied IPv6 default route pointing to unprovisioned NAT64 gateway in AZ-c (drift + missing canary). Contributing factors: no precondition on gateway healthy state, no canary for route changes, low observability on IPv6 path failures.

lisa_support: customer comms: draft message created, will send to affected customers once postmortem details finalized.

incident-bot: Incident reassigned to tina_sre. Severity downgraded to SEV3 as customer impact resolved.

maya_oncall: closing my oncall here. good work team.

tina_sre: will open postmortem ticket and include remediation actions: 1) add precondition check in Terraform to ensure gateway ID exists and is healthy before attaching IPv6 ::/0 route; 2) add canary rollout for route changes in az-c; 3) add synthetic IPv6 checks to our e2e monitors and alerting; 4) update runbook with steps for emergency delete-route and rollback.

jay_infra: noted, will add PR and link to postmortem.

incident-bot: Incident resolved. Timeline: detection 2765432199 -> mitigation 2765432234 -> handoff 2765432265 -> resolved 2765432275.

maya_oncall: closing thread. thanks all :thumbsup:
